sources.title: Rolf Strootman: Seleucid Empire
sources.note: Political history: foundation 312/311 BCE, four periods and changing hegemony; source explicitly distinguishes empire from uniform administration. Imported geometry checked separately.

sources.title: Rolf Strootman: Seleucus
sources.note: City foundations and names; avoid assigning every city in Appian list securely to Seleucus rather than Antiochus.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Seleucid Empire
sources.note: Historical survey: Parthian capture of Seleucia 141 BCE, Armenian expansion, Pompey ending remnant in 64 BCE. Do not repeat questionable battle date or exact troop totals.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: tetradrachm 1978.93.20
sources.note: Silver coin about 304 to 294 BCE, excavated Pasargadae, portrait interpreted as Seleucus with leopard skin and bull attributes, likely Susa mint.

sources.title: University of Colorado Boulder: Seleucus I tetradrachm, 296/5 BCE
sources.note: Direct university exhibit record gives Greek legend ΒΑΣΙΛΕΩΣ ΣΕΛΕΥΚΟΥ and translation of King Seleucus. Coin from John Nebel collection, reference SC I 130, plate7 130.20 variant.

sources.title: Royal Inscriptions of Babylonia online: Antiochus I 01
sources.note: Scholarly Akkadian edition BM36277, obverse6 to 15 king claims brick-moulding and foundation 27 March268 BCE; indexed full primary edition after direct error. Royal rhetoric is attributed.

sources.title: CRAST, University of Turin: Seleucia excavations
sources.note: Archives levelV, dated sealings and shelves; post129 BCE fire later than initial141 BCE Parthian conquest. Stoa levelV drainage late3rd/early2nd BCE. Public narrative does not assign Parthian houses to Seleucids.

sources.title: Australian Mission to Jebel Khalid: the Housing Insula
sources.note: Joint ANU/Melbourne excavation overview:3150 square metres,7 or8 complexes,about100rooms,mid3rdcentury toabout72BCE.

sources.title: Graeme Clarke and Heather Jackson: Jebel Khalid Twenty Years On
sources.note: Ancient History37:1(2007), printed105 bathing/toilet trough in governor residence, printed110 cooking pots and courtyard domed ovens. Small pots do not establish small households.

sources.title: Paola Corò: Seleucid Tablets from Uruk in the British Museum
sources.note: 2018 scholarly edition, printed66 to 67 temple-enterer prebends and Bēlēssunu purchases, table28 and documents77-P/78-P/82-P. Neither temple-monopoly theory nor equality for all women is asserted.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: The World between Empires, catalogue173
sources.note: Printed241 catalogue173, Uruk VAT7847, early2ndcenturyBCE, drawings Jupiter/Hydra/Leo; omens/table of associations; attribution supported by owner attested194 to 181BCE.

sources.title: Laurianne Martinez-Sève: Susa in the Hellenistic and Parthian periods
sources.note: Hellenistic urban fabric: elite house peristyle/painted panels/roof, attribution Greek-Macedonian is scholarly interpretation. Avoid broad later Parthian figure exports.
